articles.title: Cutting immigration to the UK means billions less for the Treasury. Can the country really afford that? | Zoe Williams
articles.summary:
‘Taking back control’ turns out to be staggeringly expensive. That’s something to mull over as budget day approaches

Every 100,000 immigrants lost to the UK costs the treasury £7bn, according to the Office for Budget Responsibility. That figure is unsurprising if you’ve been concentrating at all – the calculation was made in 2024 – but at the same time completely staggering. Nobody ever says, “The chancellor’s going to be in trouble because of all those lost immigrants”; few people remark on, let alone decry, the very large numbers of migrants who have been lost due to policy decisions.

And then, as budget day approaches, brute facts and mathematical realities assert themselves: migration numbers have been falling faster than anticipated. And if you take all the measures you can to discourage international students, skilled workers, all imaginable young, mobile people who work and don’t get ill, while at the same time preventing with all your might any legitimate employment opportunities for asylum seekers, you will suffer a hit to the national coffers.

articles.title: A leftwing victory in Berlin shows people want freedom, and liberals cannot deliver it | Eva von Redecker
articles.summary:
Die Linke’s surge was propelled by a compelling promise: for voters to have the freedom to stay in their city. This is how to fight back against the far right

The German leftwing party Die Linke won the state elections in Berlin on 20 September. It’s unclear whether the party will be able to form a coalition, appoint its lead candidate Elif Eralp as mayor, and follow through on her core campaign promise: to socialise the housing stock of the city’s biggest real-estate companies. A barrage of accusations started to circulate immediately after the results came in. Even by the standards of present-day polarisation, the pitch was extreme.

On the basis of one leaked chat and one rapper’s performance, the party was described as schmoozing with criminal clans and endangering the lives of Berlin Jews. Accusations of antisemitism prompted the Greens and the SPD – potential coalition partners – to question any potential cooperation, while “alt-right” opinion-makers suggested that “Hamas and Hezbollah” had won the elections, or that the German Democratic Republic (the old East Germany) was about to come back. Alice Weidel of the rightwing AfD alleged that Die Linke intended to “shoot the rich”.

articles.title: Switzerland’s love of referendums keeps the far right at bay | Joseph de Weck
articles.summary:
Brexit gave direct democracy a bad name. But the Swiss approach could be what Europe needs now

Fascism rests on a two-part confidence trick. First, a leader claims to embody the will of the people. Then they argue that only by being granted sweeping powers can that be realised. Having grown up in Switzerland, I find it easy to see through this trick. That is because the policies championed by the far right rarely pass the referendum test.

Dismantling publicly funded media? In March, 62% of Swiss voters rejected a far-right initiative to halve funding for the country’s public broadcaster. Corporate tax cuts? In 2017, 59% struck down such plans of the Swiss government. Immigration police hunting down migrants? Again, 59% rejected a far-right proposal to automatically deport foreign nationals convicted of crimes without judicial review. Or this week’s resounding 70% “No” vote on a far-right proposal to tighten Switzerland’s neutrality to the point that Bern would have been forced to drop sanctions on Russia over Ukraine.

Joseph de Weck is an associate fellow with the German Council on Foreign Relations and writes for Guardian Europe from Zürich and Paris

Britská politika pak řeší dlouhodobé ekonomické dopady brexitu a sílící debaty o budoucím směřování vztahů s EU.
archive.security_status_en: The European security landscape continues to deteriorate due to escalating Russian attacks on Ukraine's critical and digital infrastructure, sabotage incidents in Poland, and tense diplomatic talks at the UN General Assembly. Domestically, European nations face mounting social tensions, military service protests in Germany, and a deep housing affordability crisis in Spain. Meanwhile, UK politics grapples with the lingering economic costs of Brexit and intensifying debates over future ties with the EU.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující hybridní útoky na kritickou infrastrukturu a zesílení diplomatického tlaku kolem evropské obrany. Finanční trhy budou citlivě reagovat na jakékoliv náznaky další eskalace konfliktu.
archive.forecast_en: In the coming days, continued hybrid attacks on critical infrastructure and intensified diplomatic pressure surrounding European defense are expected. Financial markets will remain sensitive to any signs of further conflict escalation.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí rostoucímu vlnění politické nestability a hybridních hrozeb, včetně sabotáží kritické infrastruktury a kybernetických útoků na ukrajinská datová centra. Zatímco francouzská krajní pravice slaví historické zisky v senátu a Německo bojuje s identitární krizí a protivládními protesty, ekonomika těží z prudkého nárůstu prodejů tepelných čerpadel po energetickém šoku.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing a rising wave of political instability and hybrid threats, including critical infrastructure sabotage and cyberattacks on Ukrainian data centers. While the French far-right celebrates historic senate gains and Germany struggles with an identity crisis and protests, the economy benefits from a sharp surge in heat pump sales following the energy shock.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zostřenou rétoriku kolem sankcí vůči Rusku a další bezpečnostní opatření na ochranu evropské kritické infrastruktury. Finanční trhy budou nadále nervózně sledovat politický vývoj ve Francii a Německu.
archive.forecast_en: In the coming days, heightened rhetoric surrounding sanctions against Russia and additional security measures to protect European critical infrastructure are expected. Financial markets will continue to nervously monitor political developments in France and Germany.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí stupňujícímu se tlaku v oblasti vnitřní bezpečnosti kvůli pokračujícím ruským útokům na ukrajinskou kritickou infrastrukturu a sabotážním incidentům na vlastním území. Politická nestabilita sílí v důsledku hlubokých krizí bydlení ve Španělsku, rezignace srbského prezidenta a posunu voličů směrem k radikálním stranám v Německu a Francii.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing escalating internal security pressures due to ongoing Russian attacks on Ukrainian critical infrastructure and sabotage incidents on its own soil. Political instability is deepening amid severe housing crises in Spain, the resignation of Serbia's president, and a voter shift toward radical parties in Germany and France.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zostřenou ostrahu kritické infrastruktury a diplomatické napětí mezi Kyjevem a Soujoi. Finanční trhy budou nadále nervózně vstřebávat politické dopady volebních posunů v Německu a Francii.
archive.forecast_en: In the coming days, heightened vigilance over critical infrastructure and diplomatic tensions between Kyiv and Seoul are expected. Financial markets will continue to nervously digest the political impacts of electoral shifts in Germany and France.
